messages:
AlexW: ran a focused nsys + perfetto for the 1.5B inference path. noticed split-K kernels (cublasLtSplitK) are ~45% of GPU time when batch >= 18. workspace OOMs and fallbacks show up in the trace. attaching quick summary below.

Marta: can you paste the nsys command and the hot kernel list?

AlexW: nsys command i used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o splitk_run ./runner --batch 20 --seq 2048`
Kernel top from nsys (sorted by time):
- cublasLtMatmul algo=0 (split-K) 1.2s
- cublasLtMatmul algo=4 (batched) 0.5s
- cudaMemcpyAsync 0.2s
- custom-gemm-kernel 0.1s

SamJ: interesting — split-K spikes when seq>=1024 + batch>16, right?

AlexW: yep. baseline with batch 8 and seq 1024 shows split-K ~12% time. bumping batch makes workspace requests balloon and cuBLASLt reports workspace allocation failure (in log) so it falls back to algo with no workspace which is slower.

Ravi: do we have the cuBLASLt debug log snippet? that would confirm fallback reason.

AlexW: log snippet: `cublasLtMatmul: requestedWorkspace=6291456, got=0, status=CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED -> falling back to algo=NO_WSPACE`

Marta: hmm KV cache behaviour might amplify fragmentation: variable token lengths allocate KV slabs of different sizes causing allocator to leave holes, so subsequent matmuls see reduced contiguous workspace. anyone profiled device mem fragmentation?

SamJ: i ran `cudaMemGetInfo` snapshots in between batches — free memory drops in steps and never returns to baseline. suspect our per-request KV cache slab allocator doesn't coalesce.

AlexW: perfetto timeline shows repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree bursts aligning with request boundary. here's the timeline note: `malloc spike @ t=12.2s, free @ t=12.3s (non-coalesced), next malloc @ t=12.4s fails large contiguous alloc`

perf-bot: detected increase in matmul wall-time by 38% vs baseline (last 7 runs).

Ravi: quick mitigations: 1) cap split-K enablement to batch<=16; 2) attempt prealloc workspace slab per-device (large contiguous) and hand it to cublasLt hooks; 3) improve KV allocator to use power-of-two bins to reduce fragmentation.

Marta: agree. also think we can change batching heuristic to prefer micro-batching when seq is long: e.g., if seq>1500 prefer smaller per-request batch to keep workspace peak down.

SamJ: tested prealloc approach: reserve 64MB contiguous buffer at startup and pass pointer via `cublasLtMatmulDescriptorSetAttribute` (pseudo). result: split-K stays fast and no fallback, total matmul time down 22% for batch 20.

AlexW: exact perf numbers from that experiment: batch20/seq2048
- before: avg matmul kernel time 1.85s
- after prealloc: avg 1.44s
- per-request latency p95 improved ~160ms

Ravi: patch idea: expose env `REDWOOD_CUBLASLT_WSPACE_HINT_BYTES` to set workspace target per-device; runtime will try to satisfy or route to smaller-batch policy. less invasive.

Marta: also flag: split-K produces more concurrent kernel launches and interacts badly with our per-stream KV cache updates. we saw overlapping kernel queues causing higher register pressure on sms. perfetto heatmap shows increased occupancy variance.

SamJ: code snippet i used to force prealloc (pseudo):
```
void *wspace = cudaMallocDevice(64*1024*1024);
cublasLtMatmulDescSetAttribute(desc, CUBLASLT_MATMUL_DESC_WORKSPACE, &wspace, sizeof(void*));
```
results were promising but hacky. need proper API usage.

AlexW: next steps: 1) add clip in split-K heuristic (PR incoming), 2) prototype prealloc + env flag (Ravi), 3) run long tail test with variable seqs to reproduce fragmentation (Sam). will post PR IDs when ready.

Marta: thanks. @Ravi can you also add an nsight timeline snippet to the PR so reviewers can see heatmap differences? :thumbsup:

Ravi: on it. will attach perfetto link and nvprof kernel summary.

AlexW: cc @eng-runtime if anyone else sees similar production blips report the trace. cheers.
